analysis_purpose: Full systems analysis to validate cohesion of workflows, tools, templates, and schemas after v3.4-v3.6 updates

path_configuration.note: Meta-analysis: Reflow is both the tooling AND the system being analyzed

framework_configuration.selected_framework_rationale: Decision Flow Framework is the correct choice for Reflow meta-analysis. Workflows are fundamentally STATE MACHINES with CONDITIONAL TRANSITIONS, not service architectures. Decision Flow models: (1) Steps as states with node types (process_step, decision_node), (2) Transitions with conditions and probabilities for flow analysis, (3) Rework loops as semantic cycles, (4) Quality gates as decision nodes. This enables flow analysis to find common paths, cycle detection to measure rework probability, and path analysis to identify bottlenecks - insights UAF completely missed.
framework_configuration.note: Treating workflow steps as states in decision flow graph with conditional transitions
framework_configuration.switch_reason: UAF treated steps as services which missed decision logic, rework loops, and path probabilities. Decision Flow Framework reveals workflow dynamics.

analysis_configuration.analysis_rationale: Decision Flow Framework analysis priorities: (1) FLOW = find most-traveled paths and bottlenecks using transition probabilities, (2) CYCLES = identify rework loops (validation failures), (3) PATHS = find critical path (architecture-only) vs full development path, (4) CENTRALITY = identify critical decision nodes (quality gates), (5) COMMUNITY = detect workflow phases (Setup, Architecture, Development, Operations)
analysis_configuration.edge_weight_semantic: transition_probability (0.0-1.0) - likelihood of taking this path
analysis_configuration.note: Edge weights enable flow analysis to reveal workflow dynamics UAF missed: common vs rare paths, rework probability, bottlenecks

progress_summary.current_focus: Functional Architecture First with Mandatory Visualization (v2.1.0): Enhanced workflows to require human-readable visualizations (BPMN/UML) and stakeholder validation BEFORE system allocation
progress_summary.next_action: Workflows now enforce dual validation: (1) Stakeholder validation via visual diagrams AND (2) Technical validation via graph analysis. Machine-readable JSON alone is insufficient.

systems_engineering_methodology.philosophy: Functional Architecture First with Human Visualization - Define WHAT before HOW, and validate visually with stakeholders

phase_0.name: Functional Requirements Definition
phase_0.purpose: Extract and document functional requirements from foundational documents
phase_0.validation: Validate against user scenarios for completeness
phase_0.gate: G-SE-00A - BLOCKING until requirements complete and stakeholder-reviewed

phase_1.name: Functional Architecture Definition & Visualization
phase_1.purpose: Define complete functional architecture with MANDATORY human-readable visualizations and stakeholder validation

visualization_requirements.purpose: Enable stakeholder understanding and validation - machine-readable JSON is insufficient
visualization_requirements.standards: Use industry-standard notation (BPMN, UML), include legends, color-code traceability
visualization_requirements.for_feature_updates: Show change deltas - current vs. proposed side-by-side comparisons with changes highlighted

stakeholder_validation.outcome: Stakeholder sign-off required before proceeding to functional allocation
stakeholder_validation.iteration: Must iterate based on stakeholder feedback until approval obtained

phase_1.technical_validation: Use system_of_systems_graph_v2.py to detect gaps, redundancies, inefficiencies
phase_1.dual_validation_required: BOTH stakeholder validation (via visualizations) AND technical validation (via graph analysis) must pass
phase_1.gate: G-SE-00B or G-FU-01A - BLOCKING until functional architecture is complete, visualized, stakeholder-approved, and technically validated

phase_2.name: Functional Allocation
phase_2.purpose: Map functions to services/systems with high cohesion, low coupling
phase_2.validation: Ensure 100% functional coverage - all functions allocated to services

phase_3.name: System Architecture Definition
phase_3.purpose: Create service_architecture.json using selected framework (UAF, etc.)
phase_3.note: Services implement functions allocated in phase 2

benefits: Prevents rework from incomplete or incorrect requirements
Validates design with stakeholders BEFORE implementation using visual diagrams
Prevents costly misalignment between stakeholder expectations and implemented system
Finds architectural issues (gaps, redundancies, inefficiencies) early through dual validation (stakeholder + technical)
Ensures complete functional coverage of user scenarios
Creates well-designed service boundaries with high cohesion and low coupling
Reduces cost and time by avoiding late-stage architectural changes
Enables non-technical stakeholders to understand and validate system design through BPMN/UML diagrams
Prevents scope creep by getting stakeholder sign-off on functional architecture before allocation

lesson_learned.context: Content creation services development and general systems engineering best practices
lesson_learned.problem_1: Jumped directly to defining system 'black boxes' using UAF framework without first completing functional architecture. This caused issues later when gaps in functionality were discovered, requiring revisiting how services were initially defined.
lesson_learned.problem_2: Even when functional architecture was defined, it was often only in machine-readable JSON format, making stakeholder validation difficult or impossible. Stakeholders couldn't understand or validate the design until seeing the implemented system, leading to costly rework.
lesson_learned.root_cause_1: Skipped functional architecture phase and went straight to system allocation (defining WHICH service does WHAT instead of first defining WHAT needs to be done)
lesson_learned.root_cause_2: Treated visualization as optional documentation rather than a mandatory validation artifact. Machine-readable JSON alone is insufficient for stakeholder communication.
lesson_learned.solution: 1) Add mandatory SE-00A (Functional Requirements) and SE-00B (Functional Architecture with Visualization) steps BEFORE SE-01 (System Decomposition). 2) Make human-readable visualizations (BPMN, UML) MANDATORY, not optional. 3) Require stakeholder sign-off on visualizations before proceeding. 4) Use system_of_systems_graph_v2.py for technical analysis. 5) Iterate based on BOTH stakeholder feedback AND technical analysis.
lesson_learned.impact: Significant reduction in architectural rework, better service boundaries, complete functional coverage, stakeholder alignment throughout design process, reduced costly late-stage changes from stakeholder feedback
